text:
sana: Heads-up — I want to propose adding a new top-level field `capacity_tier` on console telemetry and ingest events. Goal: make routing + billing + per-route SLAs simpler without runtime regex lookups. Sketch below and a migration plan.

eli: +1 on the idea. Can you outline how this maps to current data model? will this be another JSONB field or separate column?

sana: Plan is: add a postgres column `capacity_tier text` to the main events table (not just JSONB) so we can index and filter efficiently for dashboards and quota calc. We'll also write a stable inference job that computes the tier for historical events based on: reserved_capacity flag, tenant plan, and most recent dedicated_assignment mapping. Backfill window = 90d to start.

mel: big questions: 1) dual-write path for new column, 2) index strategy, 3) how console will fallback when column is null during rollout.

sana: answers:
- dual-write: ingestion proxy will write both JSON payload and populate capacity_tier column. We'll deploy feature-gate and phased rollout.
- index: partial index on capacity_tier for non-null + composite idx (capacity_tier, route_id, ts DESC) to support per-route time-range queries.
- console fallback: UI will show computed tier from telemetry if column null, with a small bot alert on the metrics page during rollout.

jordan: what about billing pipeline? if we change the shape, need to ensure offline billing joins still work.

sana: billing will keep reading from events table; we'll add capacity_tier to billing ETL and have grace for missing values by using legacy heuristics for earlier rows. We'll keep a rsync between heuristics output and new column for 30 days to validate.

eli: migration plan sketch please — we need steps for safe backfill and rollback.

sana: migration steps (proposal):

1) Schema migration (no backfill): add column `capacity_tier text NULL` with DEFAULT NULL; create partial index concurrently for non-null values.
2) Ingest change: add dual-write in proxy (write column from request if present) behind gate. Deploy small canary to 5% ingest traffic.
3) Validation: spot-check canary rows, and run a sample query comparing JSONB-derived tier vs column.
4) Backfill job (read-only on production): a distributed job that updates rows in batches by ts range; mark progress to avoid repeats. Start with last 7d, then 30d, then full 90d.
5) ETL update: point billing and console queries at capacity_tier where available; keep legacy heuristics as fallback until backfill complete.
6) Index tuning: after backfill reach steady state, rebuild index with optimized fillfactor.
7) Remove gate and stop heuristics after 45 days of full backfill and confidence metrics.

mel: how do we ensure backfill doesn't bloat WAL or cause replication lag?

sana: backfill will use small batch size, UPDATE ... WHERE capacity_tier IS NULL LIMIT 1000-style loops and off-peak windows. We'll throttle and monitor replication lag via ops alerts. If lag > threshold, backfill pauses automatically.

ops: make sure to add a feature flag to the migration so we can pause/reverse the proxy writes quickly. Also we need an SLO twist — adding this column could affect p99 writes, please perf test.

telemetry-bot: NOTE: New metric idea: telemetry.capacity_tier.fill_fraction gauge for percentage of rows with non-null tier over backfill window. Add to console dashboard.

jordan: Query impacts: adding column should reduce CPU for queries that were JSONB indexing. But we might need to rewrite a few materialized views used by per-route dashboards.

eli: Are there security or PII concerns for tier? probably not. But ensure KMS metadata for private deployments isn't accidentally exposed by new ETL joins.

sana: agree. We'll run a privacy scan and add a whitelist of fields allowed in billing exports. capacity_tier is allowed.

mel: can we get a short SQL snippet for the schema migration so infra and DBAs can review?

sana: snippet:

```
-- add column with minimal lock
ALTER TABLE telemetry.events ADD COLUMN capacity_tier TEXT;
-- create partial index concurrently
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_capacity_tier_nonnull
  ON telemetry.events (capacity_tier, route_id, ts DESC)
  WHERE capacity_tier IS NOT NULL;
```

mel: looks reasonable. please add comment about NOT SETTING a DEFAULT to avoid rewrite.

sana: yup will leave DEFAULT NULL. Also will add migration telemetry tag so we can trace DB changes.

jordan: Rollout timeline suggestion: 2 weeks for canary + validation, 3 weeks for staged backfill (7d -> 30d -> 90d), then 2 weeks of monitoring. Total ~7 weeks.

eli: +1. Also add an automated reconciler that compares heuristics vs column and logs mismatches into a staging table for later review.

sana: good call — will add a reconcile job. One more: dashboards need a temporary flag to toggle between legacy and new column for comparison charts.

ops: we'll add ops runbook for backfill pause/resume and emergency rollback: steps to remove proxy dual-write & disable backfill.

telemetry-bot: ACTION: create dashboard panel: "capacity_tier backfill progress" and alert on <30% after 2 weeks.

mel: ok please open a PR with the migration SQL, proxy change, backfill job, and README for rollout. Tag DBAs and compliance. Thanks!

sana: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
